<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

Co-authors: @AichenF @jychen21 @YijiaZhao
Submitted by: [xuechengw](https://github.com/ouershua2299)

> **Dependency scope:** opt-in SM90 support that requires a FlashInfer build containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6343 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517, both merged into FlashInfer `main` (validated at `da992ed9919604c5eb6dc255c63f5e89a466452c`). The default FlashInfer `0.7.2` pin and Docker/CI dependencies remain unchanged. An older build gives an explicit load-time error only when this path is selected; every other SM90 path is unaffected. The cookbook includes a fixed-revision source-install recipe. Out-of-box support follows a coordinated FlashInfer version bump, which needs no change to this code. The branch is rebased onto main `6cac4dc3fe`.

## Motivation

On Hopper, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` covers FP8 checkpoints only. FlashInfer flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6343 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517 add `flashinfer.megamoe`, an SM90 MegaMoE kernel for NVFP4 weights with FP8 activations (dispatch, both expert GEMMs, SwiGLU and combine in one persistent kernel, with a split variant for large batches). This PR wires it into the existing `megamoe` path for ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints, starting with `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`.

On 8x H200 and 8x H20, TP8 / attention-DP8 / EP8, it is faster than DeepEP + DeepGEMM FP8 (W8A8) in prefill and decode (H200: 1.34x prefill TTFT, 1.13x decode ITL; H20: 1.27x / 1.42x) and at parity with the SM90 FP8 MegaMoE path while using NVFP4 weights.

## Modifications

1. **SM90 NVFP4 MegaMoE path** (`layers/moe/mega_moe_sm90_fi_nvfp4.py`, `layers/moe/mega_moe.py`, `layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`):
   - Converts the ModelOpt expert weights at load into the format `transform_nvfp4_weights_for_mega_moe` expects (Marlin nibble order, one global scale per expert, local scales rebalanced into the kernel's range without changing the dequantized values).
   - Forward: DeepGEMM's SM90 pre-dispatch writes FP8 activations into the FlashInfer buffer, then `commit_staged()` and `nvfp4_mega_moe`. Under DP attention every rank launches with the same padded token count, as FlashInfer requires.
   - Prewarms the FlashInfer JIT modules before CUDA-graph capture; rejects EPLB and FlashInfer builds without flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517.
2. **ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE method** (`layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`): on SM90 with `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, builds the experts through the module above.
3. **Environment variables** (`environ.py`, `environment_variables.mdx`): `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM90_PREWARM`, `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM90_KERNEL_FAMILY`.
4. **Tests**: weekly 8x H200 e2e test (cookbook launch + sgl-eval GSM8K), skipped when FlashInfer lacks flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517.
5. **Docs**: DeepSeek-V4 cookbook note with the launch command and a fixed-revision FlashInfer install.
6. **Prefill CUDA graphs** (`layers/dp_attention.py`): when the FI path is captured into a prefill graph it latches the shared-bucket flag, so every DP rank replays one MAX_LEN bucket (FlashInfer needs the same token count on every rank) and batches with an idle rank fall back to eager.

**Local CPU validation** on the branch in the CI image without GPUs: the `layers/moe`, `layers/quantization` and `server_args` unit suites show no new failures against main `6cac4dc3fe` (the same 17 GPU-dependent cases fail on both); pre-commit passed for all changed files.

**Test environment**: one host, 8x NVIDIA H200 141 GB (NVLink); image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4` with this branch on top of `6cac4dc3fe`; FlashInfer built from `main` `da992ed` as a wheel (`pip wheel "flashinfer-python @ git+https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer@da992ed..."`) and installed into the image, with no `PYTHONPATH` overlay and no disabled version checks; model `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`; sgl-eval 0.1.3. Unless noted: `--tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend megamoe`.

**Review update (rebased onto main `ca4bedfffa`).** The prefill-graph change was checked on 8x H200 (image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261025-65633129`, FlashInfer `da992ed`) with uneven DP bursts: one long request with 7 idle ranks, mixes crossing the 256-token fused/split boundary, alternating 120/600 and 150/450-token prefills one per rank, and 7 short + 1 long. Default config (eager prefill) and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`, before and after the change: no hang, GSM8K answers unchanged within noise. `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full` does not start on DeepSeek-V4 (its attention backend does not capture EXTEND), with or without this PR.

**Dependency compatibility.** With the image's released FlashInfer `0.7.2` wheel (no `flashinfer.megamoe`), selecting this path raises the expected load-time error naming flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6343 / flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517, the new e2e test skips (8 skipped), and the unit suites above behave as on main.

## Accuracy Tests

Registered tests on the environment above:

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/e2e/models/test_deepseek_v4_flash_nvfp4_megamoe_h200.py
```

```text
8 passed in 545.37s           # e2e (8xH200), GSM8K gate 0.975
```

**GSM8K** with the registered `GSM8KMixin` settings (`sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 128 --no-thinking`, sgl-eval 0.1.3), the cookbook command for this PR and the launch commands below for the baselines, 8x H200:

| Backend | Checkpoint | GSM8K |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| FlashInfer SM90 NVFP4 MegaMoE (this PR) | `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` | 0.965 |
| DeepEP + DeepGEMM FP8 (W8A8) | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` | 0.975 |
| SM90 FP8 MegaMoE | `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8` | 0.980 |

Across the runs of this PR (cookbook launch and the e2e gate, before and after rebasing) GSM8K ranged 0.965-0.980.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 8x H200 and 8x H20-3e, TP8 / attention-DP8 / EP8, decode CUDA graphs on, `sglang.bench_serving` random dataset with fixed lengths (`--random-range-ratio 1`), seed 20260811, warmup requests equal to the concurrency, cache flushed between cases, median of 3 runs per point. Ratios are FlashInfer MegaMoE over the baseline, geometric mean over input <= 8k and concurrency <= 256; > 1 means FlashInfer is better.

| Metric | H200 vs DeepEP+DeepGEMM FP8 | H200 vs DeepEP+Humming W4A8 | H200 vs SM90 FP8 MegaMoE | H20 vs DeepEP+DeepGEMM FP8 | H20 vs DeepEP+Humming W4A8 | H20 vs SM90 FP8 MegaMoE |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill-only input throughput | 1.29 | 1.37 † | 0.97 | 1.20 | 1.22 | 1.01 |
| Prefill-only TTFT | 1.34 | 1.41 † | 0.98 | 1.27 | 1.30 | 1.01 |

### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `232e96a`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45613/checks?check_run_id=121167995725)

(From GPT6)
[P1] Uneven DP prefill CUDA graph replay violates FlashInfer’s cross-rank contract
_rank_invariant_tokens() returns the local graph’s token count during capture. However, prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len() still allows MegaMoE ranks to replay different prefill graph buckets. For example, ranks replaying 128-token and 512-token graphs would launch the fused and split kernel families respectively, while FlashInfer requires all ranks to use the same token count and matching kernels. This mismatch can cause collective hangs or incorrect execution.

Please enforce a shared prefill graph bucket across all EP ranks for this backend, or temporarily reject this configuration. Regression coverage should include uneven token counts, idle ranks, and buckets crossing the fused/split boundary.

@Fridge003 Thanks for the review. We could not reproduce a hang or wrong output from uneven prefill graph replay on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but the concern is valid against FlashInfer's contract (same token count on every EP rank), so we changed it as you suggested in 232e96a466:

- While the FI NVFP4 MegaMoE path is captured into a prefill graph, it now latches the existing shared-bucket flag (the same one a captured DP gather sets, via a new `note_shared_bucket_in_prefill_graph()` in `dp_attention.py`). `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len()` then returns False, so every DP rank replays one MAX_LEN bucket, and batches with an idle rank fall back to eager, where this path already pads to the gathered max token count. Decode graphs already replay one shared bucket on all DP ranks, and the default config (prefill graphs disabled) is unchanged.

Test setup: 8x H200, branch rebased onto main `ca4bedfffa`, image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261025-65633129`, FlashInfer `da992ed`, `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`, cookbook flags. The client sends concurrent GSM8K prompts padded to different lengths so DP ranks get uneven token counts in the same step: 1 long request with 7 idle ranks, 3 / 8 / 20 mixed lengths crossing the 256-token fused/split boundary, 120/600 and 150/450 tokens alternating one per rank, 7 short + 1 long, and 1 short request.

| Prefill graph | Before (5e5c94985e) | After (232e96a466) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| disabled (default) | pass, 2 rounds | pass, 2 rounds, same answers |
| `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` | pass, 2 + 5 rounds, ranks replay per-rank buckets | pass, 2 + 5 rounds, all ranks log the shared MAX_LEN bucket |
| `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full` | fails at startup | fails at startup |

"pass" means no request timed out (no cross-rank hang) and greedy GSM8K answers stayed within noise (e.g., 150/450 alternating: 13-16/16 before, 14-16/16 after). With `full`, DeepSeek-V4's attention backend raises `NotImplementedError: unsupported forward_mode=EXTEND` during prefill graph capture, before the MoE runs, so `breakable` is the reachable prefill-graph path for this model. Our guess for why the old behavior did not fail: in the observed steps the ranks replaying graphs mostly landed above 256 tokens, where they select the same split plan even with different M.

Thanks for keeping the FlashInfer megamoe wiring explicit (source build with #6343/#6517, not PyPI 0.7.2).

Our offline DeepInfer Hopper fork stays on DeepEP V2 + humming for stock MXFP4 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and will not vendor flashinfer.megamoe. flashinfer#6999 has now merged on the separate moe_ep NVFP4×FP8 surface; we treat that as a watch item too, still without a CUDA drop. Once this PR merges we can re-test on H200 against a humming JSONL, only for a ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint if we actually have one.

Question: after #6999 landed, should this PR stay on flashinfer.megamoe (#6517), or do you intend to move Hopper NVFP4 MegaMoE over to moe_ep?

FlashInfer flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6343 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517 add `flashinfer.megamoe`, an SM90 MegaMoE kernel for NVFP4 weights with FP8 activations (dispatch, both expert GEMMs, SwiGLU and combine in one persistent kernel, with a split variant for large batches). This PR wires it into the existing `megamoe` path for ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints, starting with `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`.

On 8x H200 and 8x H20, TP8 / attention-DP8 / EP8, it is faster than DeepEP + DeepGEMM FP8 (W8A8) in prefill and decode (H200: 1.34x prefill TTFT, 1.13x decode ITL; H20: 1.27x / 1.42x) and at parity with the SM90 FP8 MegaMoE path while using NVFP4 weights.

## Modifications

1. **SM90 NVFP4 MegaMoE path** (`layers/moe/mega_moe_sm90_fi_nvfp4.py`, `layers/moe/mega_moe.py`, `layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py`):
   - Converts the ModelOpt expert weights at load into the format `transform_nvfp4_weights_for_mega_moe` expects (Marlin nibble order, one global scale per expert, local scales rebalanced into the kernel's range without changing the dequantized values).
   - Forward: DeepGEMM's SM90 pre-dispatch writes FP8 activations into the FlashInfer buffer, then `commit_staged()` and `nvfp4_mega_moe`. Under DP attention every rank launches with the same padded token count, as FlashInfer requires.
   - Prewarms the FlashInfer JIT modules before CUDA-graph capture; rejects EPLB and FlashInfer builds without flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517.
2. **ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE method** (`layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`): on SM90 with `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, builds the experts through the module above.
3. **Environment variables** (`environ.py`, `environment_variables.mdx`): `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM90_PREWARM`, `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM90_KERNEL_FAMILY`.
4. **Tests**: weekly 8x H200 e2e test (cookbook launch + sgl-eval GSM8K), skipped when FlashInfer lacks flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517.
5. **Docs**: DeepSeek-V4 cookbook note with the launch command and a fixed-revision FlashInfer install.
6. **Prefill CUDA graphs** (`layers/dp_attention.py`): when the FI path is captured into a prefill graph it latches the shared-bucket flag, so every DP rank replays one MAX_LEN bucket (FlashInfer needs the same token count on every rank) and batches with an idle rank fall back to eager.

**Test environment**: one host, 8x NVIDIA H200 141 GB (NVLink); image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4` with this branch on top of `6cac4dc3fe`; FlashInfer built from `main` `da992ed` as a wheel (`pip wheel "flashinfer-python @ git+https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer@da992ed..."`) and installed into the image, with no `PYTHONPATH` overlay and no disabled version checks; model `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`; sgl-eval 0.1.3. Unless noted: `--tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend megamoe`.

**Review update (rebased onto main `ca4bedfffa`).** The prefill-graph change was checked on 8x H200 (image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261025-65633129`, FlashInfer `da992ed`) with uneven DP bursts: one long request with 7 idle ranks, mixes crossing the 256-token fused/split boundary, alternating 120/600 and 150/450-token prefills one per rank, and 7 short + 1 long. Default config (eager prefill) and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`, before and after the change: no hang, GSM8K answers unchanged within noise. `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full` does not start on DeepSeek-V4 (its attention backend does not capture EXTEND), with or without this PR.

## Scope and Limitations

- SM90 only, opt-in through `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` with ModelOpt NVFP4 experts. The integration is not DeepSeek-V4-specific: it uses the generic MegaMoE hook, and FlashInfer plans any legal geometry (tuned for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro and MiMo-V2.5-Pro). It needs a model with a SwiGLU limit (the kernel's clamped SwiGLU) and has been validated only on `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`.
- Against DeepEP + Humming W4A8 with humming-kernels 0.1.18 on H200, prefill is faster (1.41x TTFT) but decode above 4 tokens per rank is 3-9% slower.
- EPLB is not supported on this path.

+"""SM90 NVFP4 W4A8 MegaMoE through flashinfer.megamoe.
+
+ModelOpt NVFP4 expert tensors are converted at load into the input FlashInfer's
+transform_nvfp4_weights_for_mega_moe expects (Marlin byte order, local scales the
+decoder can hold, one global scale per expert). The forward quantizes activations to
+FP8 (group 128) with DeepGEMM's SM90 pre-dispatch kernel straight into the FlashInfer
+symmetric buffer, then calls flashinfer.megamoe.nvfp4_mega_moe (fused up to
+FAMILY_THRESHOLD tokens per rank, split above).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention import (
+    get_dp_global_num_tokens,
+    is_dp_attention_enabled,
+    note_shared_bucket_in_prefill_graph,
+)
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner import get_is_capture_mode
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_FI_SYMM_BUFFERS: dict = {}
+_DISPATCH_GROUP_SIZE = 128
+# The SM90 decoder turns FP4 * local scale into one E4M3 byte: 6 * scale <= 448.
+_MAX_LOCAL_SCALE = 448.0 / 6.0
+
+
+def is_sm90_fi_nvfp4_mega_moe_available(experts) -> bool:
+    return experts._mega_moe_sm90_fi_nvfp4
+
+
+def _require_flashinfer_megamoe() -> None:
+    try:
+        from flashinfer.megamoe import MegaMoESymmBuffer
+    except ImportError as e:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "--moe-a2a-backend megamoe on SM90 with NVFP4 experts needs a FlashInfer "
+            "build with flashinfer.megamoe (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6343 and #6517); "
+            "the installed FlashInfer does not provide it."
+        ) from e
+    if not hasattr(MegaMoESymmBuffer, "commit_staged"):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "SM90 NVFP4 MegaMoE needs FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6517 "
+            "(MegaMoESymmBuffer.prewarm / commit_staged)."
+        )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Weights: ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint -> flashinfer.megamoe input
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _low_nibble_first_to_marlin(packed: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Checkpoints store K[2i] in the low nibble of byte i; FlashInfer expects
+    # K[b] (high) | K[b + 4] (low) in byte b of each four-byte word.
+    words = packed.reshape(*packed.shape[:-1], -1, 4)
+    codes = torch.stack((words & 15, words >> 4), dim=-1).flatten(-2)
+    return ((codes[..., :4] << 4) | codes[..., 4:]).reshape(packed.shape)
+
+
+def _rebalance_scales(
+    scale: torch.Tensor, global_scale: torch.Tensor, gated: bool
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Per expert, move a power of two from the E4M3 local scales into the FP32
+    global scale until 6 * local <= 448; gate / up globals fold into one."""
+    local = scale.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()
+    global_scale = global_scale.float()
+    if gated and global_scale.dim() == 2:
+        merged = global_scale.amax(dim=1)
+        ratio = global_scale / merged[:, None]
+        n = local.shape[1] // 2
+        local = torch.cat(
+            (
+                local[:, :n] * ratio[:, 0, None, None],
+                local[:, n:] * ratio[:, 1, None, None],
+            ),
+            dim=1,
+        )
+        global_scale = merged
+    shift = torch.exp2(
+        torch.ceil(torch.log2(local.amax(dim=(1, 2)) / _MAX_LOCAL_SCALE)).clamp_min(0)
+    )
+    local = local / shift[:, None, None]
+    encoded = local.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    if not torch.equal(encoded.float(), local):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "NVFP4 expert scales cannot be rebalanced into the SM90 MegaMoE decoder "
+            "range exactly; the per-expert scale range is too wide"
+        )
+    return encoded.view(torch.uint8), (global_scale * shift).contiguous()
+
+
+def convert_nvfp4_experts_for_fi(w13, s13, g13, w2, s2, g2):
+    """Returns (l1_weights, l2_weights, l1_global_scales, l2_global_scales)."""
+    from flashinfer.megamoe import transform_nvfp4_weights_for_mega_moe
+
+    s13, g13 = _rebalance_scales(s13, g13, gated=True)
+    s2, g2 = _rebalance_scales(s2, g2, gated=False)
+    l1_w, l2_w = transform_nvfp4_weights_for_mega_moe(
+        (_low_nibble_first_to_marlin(w13.view(torch.uint8)), s13),
+        (_low_nibble_first_to_marlin(w2.view(torch.uint8)), s2),
+    )
+    return l1_w, l2_w, g13, g2
+
+
+def build_sm90_fi_nvfp4_mega_moe_experts_weights(experts) -> None:
+    if experts._mega_moe_weights_built:
+        return
+    if get_exec().moe.enable_eplb:
+        # The packed weights live outside the expert parameters EPLB rebalances.
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SM90 NVFP4 MegaMoE (--moe-a2a-backend megamoe) does not support EPLB; "
+            "disable --enable-eplb."
+        )
+    _require_flashinfer_megamoe()
+    l1_w, l2_w, l1_g, l2_g = convert_nvfp4_experts_for_fi(
+        experts.w13_weight.data,
+        experts.w13_weight_scale.data,
+        experts.w13_weight_scale_2.data,
+        experts.w2_weight.data,
+        experts.w2_weight_scale.data,
+        experts.w2_weight_scale_2.data,
+    )
+    experts.mega_l1_weights = l1_w
+    experts.mega_l2_weights = l2_w
+    experts.mega_l1_global_scales = l1_g
+    experts.mega_l2_global_scales = l2_g
+    # MegaMoE is the only consumer of the expert weights from here on.
+    for param in (
+        experts.w13_weight,
+        experts.w2_weight,
+        experts.w13_weight_scale,
+        experts.w2_weight_scale,
+    ):
+        param.data = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.uint8, device=l1_w.device)
+    experts._mega_moe_sm90_fi_nvfp4 = True
+    experts._mega_moe_weights_built = True
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Forward
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _get_fi_symm_buffer(
+    group, *, num_experts, cap, top_k, hidden, intermediate, activation_clamp
+):
+    key = (id(group), num_experts, cap, top_k, hidden, intermediate, activation_clamp)
+    buf = _FI_SYMM_BUFFERS.get(key)
+    if buf is None:
+        from flashinfer.megamoe import MegaMoESymmBuffer
+
+        buf = MegaMoESymmBuffer(
+            group,
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            num_max_tokens_per_rank=cap,
+            num_topk=top_k,
+            hidden=hidden,
+            intermediate_hidden=intermediate,
+            activation_clamp=activation_clamp,
+            fast_math=True,
+        )
+        if envs.SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM90_PREWARM.get():
+            num_modules = buf.prewarm(
+                kernel_family=envs.SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM90_KERNEL_FAMILY.get()
+            )
+            logger.info("FI_MEGAMOE_PREWARM built %d modules", num_modules)
+        _FI_SYMM_BUFFERS[key] = buf
+    return buf
+
+
+def _rank_invariant_tokens(num_tokens: int) -> int:
+    # Plan/family selection keys on M, so every EP rank must launch with the same M.
+    # Graphs bake M in at capture, so all DP ranks must replay one shared bucket.
+    if get_is_capture_mode():
+        note_shared_bucket_in_prefill_graph()
+        return num_tokens
+    if not is_dp_attention_enabled():
+        return num_tokens
+    global_num_tokens = get_dp_global_num_tokens()
+    if not global_num_tokens:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "FI MegaMoE under DP attention needs the gathered global_num_tokens"
+        )
+    m = max(global_num_tokens)
+    if num_tokens > m:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"local M={num_tokens} exceeds gathered max M={m}")
+    return m
+
+
+def run_sm90_fi_nvfp4_mega_routed(
+    experts,
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+    num_tokens: int,
+    *,
+    ep_group,
+    num_max_tokens_per_rank: int,
+    hidden_size: int,
+    intermediate_size: int,
+    top_k: int,
+    activation_clamp: Optional[float],
+    routed_scaling_factor: float,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    import deep_gemm
+    import flashinfer.megamoe as fm
+
+    if activation_clamp is None:
+        # The kernel always clamps SwiGLU; there is no unclamped variant.
+        raise ValueError("SM90 NVFP4 MegaMoE needs the model's swiglu_limit")
+    buf = _get_fi_symm_buffer(
+        ep_group,
+        num_experts=experts.num_experts,
+        cap=num_max_tokens_per_rank,
+        top_k=top_k,
+        hidden=hidden_size,
+        intermediate=intermediate_size,
+        activation_clamp=float(activation_clamp),
+    )
+    m = _rank_invariant_tokens(num_tokens)
+    if m == 0:
+        return hidden_states.new_empty((0, hidden_size))
+
+    x = hidden_states if hidden_states.is_contiguous() else hidden_states.contiguous()
+    ids = topk_ids.to(torch.int32)
+    weights = topk_weights.to(torch.float32)
+    if m > num_tokens:
+        # Padded rows route nowhere (-1) and carry zero weight; FlashInfer masks -1 routes.
+        pad_x = x.new_zeros((m, hidden_size))
+        pad_ids = ids.new_full((m, top_k), -1)
+        pad_w = weights.new_zeros((m, top_k))
+        if num_tokens:
+            pad_x[:num_tokens].copy_(x)
+            pad_ids[:num_tokens].copy_(ids)
+            pad_w[:num_tokens].copy_(weights)
+        x, ids, weights = pad_x, pad_ids, pad_w
+
+    deep_gemm.mega_moe_pre_dispatch_sm90(
+        x,
+        ids,
+        weights,
+        buf.x,
+        buf.x_sf,
+        buf.topk_idx,
+        buf.topk_weights,
+        num_tokens=m,
+        group_size=_DISPATCH_GROUP_SIZE,
+        routed_scaling_factor=routed_scaling_factor,
+    )
+    buf.commit_staged(m)
+    y = torch.empty((m, hidden_size), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=hidden_states.device)
+    fm.nvfp4_mega_moe(
+        y,
+        experts.mega_l1_weights,
+        experts.mega_l2_weights,
+        buf,
+        num_tokens=m,
+        l1_global_scales=experts.mega_l1_global_scales,
+        l2_global_scales=experts.mega_l2_global_scales,
+        kernel_family=envs.SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM90_KERNEL_FAMILY.get(),
+    )
+    return y[:num_tokens]

[P1] Uneven DP prefill CUDA graph replay violates FlashInfer’s cross-rank contract
_rank_invariant_tokens() returns the local graph’s token count during capture. However, prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len() still allows MegaMoE ranks to replay different prefill graph buckets. For example, ranks replaying 128-token and 512-token graphs would launch the fused and split kernel families respectively, while FlashInfer requires all ranks to use the same token count and matching kernels. This mismatch can cause collective hangs or incorrect execution.

Please enforce a shared prefill graph bucket across all EP ranks for this backend, or temporarily reject this configuration. Regression coverage should include uneven token counts, idle ranks, and buckets crossing the fused/split boundary.

@Fridge003 Thanks for the review. We could not reproduce a hang or wrong output from uneven prefill graph replay on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but the concern is valid against FlashInfer's contract (same token count on every EP rank), so we changed it as you suggested in 232e96a466:

- While the FI NVFP4 MegaMoE path is captured into a prefill graph, it now latches the existing shared-bucket flag (the same one a captured DP gather sets, via a new `note_shared_bucket_in_prefill_graph()` in `dp_attention.py`). `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len()` then returns False, so every DP rank replays one MAX_LEN bucket, and batches with an idle rank fall back to eager, where this path already pads to the gathered max token count. Decode graphs already replay one shared bucket on all DP ranks, and the default config (prefill graphs disabled) is unchanged.

Test setup: 8x H200, branch rebased onto main `ca4bedfffa`, image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261025-65633129`, FlashInfer `da992ed`, `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4`, cookbook flags. The client sends concurrent GSM8K prompts padded to different lengths so DP ranks get uneven token counts in the same step: 1 long request with 7 idle ranks, 3 / 8 / 20 mixed lengths crossing the 256-token fused/split boundary, 120/600 and 150/450 tokens alternating one per rank, 7 short + 1 long, and 1 short request.

| Prefill graph | Before (5e5c94985e) | After (232e96a466) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| disabled (default) | pass, 2 rounds | pass, 2 rounds, same answers |
| `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` | pass, 2 + 5 rounds, ranks replay per-rank buckets | pass, 2 + 5 rounds, all ranks log the shared MAX_LEN bucket |
| `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full` | fails at startup | fails at startup |

"pass" means no request timed out (no cross-rank hang) and greedy GSM8K answers stayed within noise (e.g., 150/450 alternating: 13-16/16 before, 14-16/16 after). With `full`, DeepSeek-V4's attention backend raises `NotImplementedError: unsupported forward_mode=EXTEND` during prefill graph capture, before the MoE runs, so `breakable` is the reachable prefill-graph path for this model. Our guess for why the old behavior did not fail: in the observed steps the ranks replaying graphs mostly landed above 256 tokens, where they select the same split plan even with different M.

Thanks for keeping the FlashInfer megamoe wiring explicit (source build with #6343/#6517, not PyPI 0.7.2).

Our offline DeepInfer Hopper fork stays on DeepEP V2 + humming for stock MXFP4 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and will not vendor flashinfer.megamoe. flashinfer#6999 has now merged on the separate moe_ep NVFP4×FP8 surface; we treat that as a watch item too, still without a CUDA drop. Once this PR merges we can re-test on H200 against a humming JSONL, only for a ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint if we actually have one.
